plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Cup-shaped blooms in saturated jewel tones rise on sturdy stems above blue-green leaves. They fill the fields and borders of the Netherlands with ribbons of color.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring, typically April to early May in the Netherlands, with peak fields in mid to late April
plants.location: Lisse and the bulb region of the Netherlands, Northern Europe
plants.funFact: In 17th-century Holland, rare tulip bulbs sold for more than the price of a grand canal house during the famous 'tulip mania'.

plants.name: Wisteria floribunda
plants.description: Long, fragrant chains of pea-like flowers hang from twisting woody vines. They form shimmering lavender curtains over pergolas and temple gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-April to mid-May in much of Japan, with peak bloom often in late April
plants.location: Honshu, Japan, including gardens such as the Ashikaga Flower Park
plants.funFact: Japanese wisteria twines clockwise around its support, while Chinese wisteria twines counterclockwise.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: Before its heart-shaped leaves unfurl, the bare branches of this small tree are covered in clusters of magenta-pink flowers. Blooms even sprout directly from the trunk.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to late April, depending on latitude, and still blooming in the cooler northern parts of its range around April 24
plants.location: Eastern and central United States, from the Appalachians to the Midwest
plants.funFact: Its flowers are edible and slightly tangy, and the habit of flowering straight from old wood is called cauliflory.
